notes: This contract records Umbra's bounded execution-scoped handle-normalization behavior. The registry owns opaque stable coordinates for handle types and preserves equality for equal designators; the adapter validates the standard connection, membership, and invalid-designator boundaries. The MIM's HLAserviceGroup dimension is bounded to seven, so the official ServiceGroup indicator is returned as its in-domain point coordinate. The five service-opening candidates have known Requirements Lab clause-attribution drift; their immutable IDs and exported clause IDs are intentionally retained here for checker compatibility, while RL-033 records the source sections. The native HLA_IMMEDIATE companion now decodes five successful type-6 service reports with official supplied and returned argument forms. This is source/test traceability only; it does not prove general DDM semantics, distributed execution, package/JUnit/protected-review evidence, or conformance.
